newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB confirms Accor sale, cap gain over two bln Bfr.
newsitem.headline: SGB confirms Accor sale, cap gain over two bln Bfr.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) confirmed on Wednesday it was selling shares in French hotel group Accor for a capital gain of over two billion Belgian francs.
French fund managers had earlier said that SGB was selling its stake in Accor at 756 francs per share. That compared with a market price of 768 at 1600 GMT, the Paris market's close.

SGB said in a statement it concluded a deal with SBC Warburg on the sale of nine percent in Accor, under which SBC would allow major institutional investors, particularly in the UK and U.S., to buy Accor stock.
Income from the deal would be booked in 1997 accounts.
SGB said the sale was in line with its strategy of focusing on core shareholdings included in its consolidated balance sheet. The deal would strengthen and promote the expansion of Accord.
SGB's chief executive officer Etienne Davignon would remain on Accor's supervisory board.
SGB is controlled by French holding company Cie. de Suez .
